Accuracy.en: The proportion of all predictions that were correct
Accuracy.zh: 準確率：所有預測中正確的比例
Accuracy.analogy: Out of all patients the model evaluated, how many did it get right?
Accuracy.matters: Best used when classes are balanced. Can be misleading with imbalanced datasets.

ROC-AUC.en: Area Under the ROC Curve — measures how well the model separates classes across all thresholds
ROC-AUC.zh: ROC-AUC：衡量模型在所有閾值下區分類別的能力
ROC-AUC.analogy: Imagine sliding the 'sensitivity dial' from 0 to max — AUC measures total performance across all settings
ROC-AUC.matters: Use for overall discrimination quality. Less affected by class imbalance than accuracy.

Precision.en: Of all cases the model flagged as positive, how many actually were positive
Precision.zh: 精確率：模型標記為陽性的案例中實際為陽性的比例
Precision.analogy: If the model says 'this patient has cancer', how often is it right?
Precision.matters: Critical when false positives are costly (unnecessary surgery, patient anxiety).

Recall.en: Of all actual positive cases, how many did the model correctly identify
Recall.zh: 召回率：實際陽性案例中被模型正確識別的比例
Recall.analogy: Of all patients who truly have cancer, how many does the model catch?
Recall.matters: Critical when missing a case is dangerous (cancer screening, disease detection).

Sensitivity.en: Same as Recall — the proportion of actual positives correctly identified
Sensitivity.zh: 靈敏度：與召回率相同，實際陽性中被正確識別的比例
Sensitivity.analogy: A highly sensitive test rarely misses real cases — it catches almost everyone who is sick
Sensitivity.matters: Essential for screening tests where missing a diagnosis has severe consequences.

Specificity.en: Of all actual negative cases, how many did the model correctly identify as negative
Specificity.zh: 特異度：實際陰性案例中被正確識別為陰性的比例
Specificity.analogy: A highly specific test rarely raises false alarms — healthy patients are correctly cleared
Specificity.matters: Important when false alarms cause harm (unnecessary biopsies, patient distress).

F1-Score.en: The harmonic mean of precision and recall — balances both types of errors
F1-Score.zh: F1 分數：精確率和召回率的調和平均數
F1-Score.analogy: A combined score that penalizes models that are good at one but bad at the other
F1-Score.matters: Best single metric when you need to balance catching cases vs. avoiding false alarms.

MCC.en: Matthews Correlation Coefficient — a balanced metric accounting for all four confusion matrix cells
MCC.zh: MCC：馬修斯相關係數，考慮混淆矩陣所有四個單元格的平衡指標
MCC.analogy: The fairest single number for classification quality — works even when classes are very unbalanced
MCC.matters: Most reliable single metric for imbalanced datasets. Ranges from -1 (worst) to +1 (perfect).

SHAP.en: SHapley Additive exPlanations — a method to explain which features drove each prediction
SHAP.zh: SHAP：一種基於特徵重要性來解釋個別預測的方法
SHAP.analogy: Like asking 'which symptoms contributed most to this diagnosis?' for each individual patient
SHAP.matters: Essential for model interpretability and clinical trust.

Confusion Matrix.en: A table showing the counts of correct and incorrect predictions for each class
Confusion Matrix.zh: 混淆矩陣：顯示每個類別正確和錯誤預測數量的表格
Confusion Matrix.analogy: A scorecard showing exactly where the model got things right and wrong
Confusion Matrix.matters: The most detailed view of model errors — shows false positives and false negatives separately.

False Positives.en: Healthy cases incorrectly flagged as abnormal by the model
False Positives.zh: 偽陽性：被模型錯誤標記為異常的健康案例
False Positives.analogy: The model says 'cancer detected' but the patient is actually healthy — a false alarm
False Positives.matters: Leads to unnecessary follow-up procedures, patient anxiety, and wasted resources.

False Negatives.en: Abnormal cases that the model failed to detect
False Negatives.zh: 偽陰性：模型未能檢測到的異常案例
False Negatives.analogy: The model says 'all clear' but the patient actually has cancer — a missed diagnosis
False Negatives.matters: The most dangerous error in screening — patients with real conditions go untreated.

Overfitting.en: When a model performs well on training data but poorly on new, unseen data
Overfitting.zh: 過擬合：模型在訓練數據上表現良好但在新數據上表現不佳
Overfitting.analogy: Like a student who memorizes the answer key but can't solve new problems
Overfitting.matters: A model that overfits will fail in real clinical deployment.

Cross-Validation.en: Repeated train/test splitting to estimate model performance more reliably
Cross-Validation.zh: 交叉驗證：重複訓練/測試分割以更可靠地估計模型性能
Cross-Validation.analogy: Testing the model multiple times on different patient groups to make sure results aren't a fluke
Cross-Validation.matters: More trustworthy than a single train/test split, especially with small datasets.

Data Leakage.en: When information from the test set accidentally influences the training process
Data Leakage.zh: 數據洩漏：測試集的信息意外影響訓練過程
Data Leakage.analogy: Like a student who accidentally sees the exam questions before the test — inflated performance
Data Leakage.matters: If detected, all performance metrics are unreliable and the model must be retrained.

Feature Selection.en: Choosing the most informative input variables to improve model performance
Feature Selection.zh: 特徵選擇：選擇最具信息量的輸入變量以提高模型性能
Feature Selection.analogy: Like a doctor deciding which lab tests are actually useful vs. which are noise
Feature Selection.matters: Reduces complexity, improves interpretability, and can prevent overfitting.

Class Imbalance.en: When one class has significantly more samples than another in the dataset
Class Imbalance.zh: 類別不平衡：數據集中某一類別的樣本明顯多於另一類別
Class Imbalance.analogy: If 95% of patients are healthy, the model can get 95% accuracy by always predicting 'healthy'
Class Imbalance.matters: Makes accuracy misleading. Use F1, MCC, AUC, and per-class metrics instead.

Threshold Tuning.en: Adjusting the decision boundary to optimize for a specific metric (e.g., sensitivity vs. specificity)
Threshold Tuning.zh: 閾值調整：調整決策邊界以優化特定指標
Threshold Tuning.analogy: Setting how cautious the alarm system should be — too sensitive and you get false alarms, too lenient and you miss real threats
Threshold Tuning.matters: Default threshold (0.5) is rarely optimal for clinical applications.

PCA.en: Principal Component Analysis — a dimensionality reduction technique that finds the axes of maximum variance
PCA.zh: PCA：主成分分析，一種找到最大方差軸的降維技術
PCA.analogy: Compressing a 3D object into a 2D shadow that preserves the most important shape information
PCA.matters: Useful for visualizing high-dimensional data and detecting natural clusters.

UMAP.en: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection — a nonlinear dimensionality reduction for visualization
UMAP.zh: UMAP：均勻流形近似與投影，一種非線性降維可視化技術
UMAP.analogy: Like arranging photos by visual similarity on a table — similar items cluster together
UMAP.matters: Better at preserving local structure than PCA. Reveals subgroups in the data.

PR Curve.en: Precision-Recall Curve — shows the tradeoff between precision and recall at different thresholds
PR Curve.zh: PR 曲線：顯示不同閾值下精確率和召回率之間的權衡
PR Curve.analogy: As you try harder to catch all real cases (recall), you inevitably flag more false alarms (lower precision)
PR Curve.matters: More informative than ROC for imbalanced datasets where the positive class is rare.

R².en: Coefficient of determination — how much of the target variability the model explains (0 to 1)
R².zh: R²：決定係數，模型解釋的目標變異性比例（0 到 1）
R².analogy: If R² = 0.85, the model explains 85% of why outcomes differ between patients
R².matters: Primary metric for regression tasks. Higher is better; negative means worse than the average.

RMSE.en: Root Mean Squared Error — the average prediction error in the same units as the target
RMSE.zh: RMSE：均方根誤差，與目標相同單位的平均預測誤差
RMSE.analogy: On average, the model's prediction is off by this much
RMSE.matters: Penalizes large errors more than small ones. Compare to the target's natural range.
